mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has risen from 6.6 to 10.1 to 11.9 percent above baseline over the last three weekly means, signaling an outdoor-activity revival that spills into retail and recreation footfall in Manhattan over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: If PARKS continues above +10 percent change from baseline but the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is not higher than the prior 28-day mean, the spillover mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has crossed from -33.6 to -29.1 to -28.0 percent change from baseline; sustained TRANSIT above -30 indicates commuter recovery that lifts weekday retail and recreation footfall over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean crosses above -30.0 percent change from baseline.
failure_condition: After TRANSIT crosses above -30, RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Joint improvement in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT, from -41.6 to -33.9 and -33.6 to -28.0 respectively, signals returning office and commuter routines that jointly boost RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: When both WORKPLACES > -35 and TRANSIT > -30 hold, RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days fails to exceed its prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility remaining above +5 percent change from baseline indicates persistent stay-at-home behavior that suppresses retail and recreation trips, pushing RETAIL_REC lower over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean stays above +5.0 for two consecutive weeks.
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL remains above +5 for two weeks yet RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than the prior 28-day mean, the suppression claim is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Early-summer seasonality, evidenced by PARKS rising to 11.9 percent above baseline, increases outdoor recreation and tourist activity that lifts RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If PARKS rises but the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is not above the prior 28-day mean, seasonal spillover is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A restrictive-policy regime keeps TRANSIT and WORKPLACES deeply negative; if TRANSIT < -28 and WORKPLACES < -34 persist, capacity limits and office closures suppress RETAIL_REC over the next week.
failure_condition: If TRANSIT < -28 and WORKPLACES < -34 persist but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days rises above the prior 28-day mean, the policy-suppression hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM normalization from -28.1 to -24.0 to -24.6 percent change from baseline signals recovering routine errands that spill into adjacent retail and recreation activity over the next week.
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM remains above -25 but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the prior 28-day mean, the errand-spillover mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of PARKS > +10 and RESIDENTIAL < +6 shows consumers are outdoors and less home-bound, creating a summer-reopening interaction that raises RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If PARKS > +10 and RESIDENTIAL < +6 both hold but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not above the prior 28-day mean, the interaction claim is rejected.
